stemMd: A planner argues that a digital archive needs periodic migration to new file formats, just as a physical archive needs periodic building maintenance. Which fact most strengthens the analogy?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Digital files can be copied rapidly.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Without periodic intervention, both archives can become unusable even when their contents are not deliberately altered.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Some archivists work with both kinds of collections.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Digital archives usually occupy less floor space.

explanationMd: An effective analogy connects the feature that supports the recommendation. Here, both systems risk losing usability without periodic work; their different physical sizes and copying speeds do not address that need.

distractorRationale.d: Access fees do not establish deterioration without maintenance.
distractorRationale.c: Shared staff does not establish a shared underlying vulnerability.
distractorRationale.a: Ease of copying is a difference rather than the relevant similarity.
distractorRationale.e: Physical size is irrelevant to the shared maintenance need.
